q: Chaitin's Ω = Σ_{p: U(p) halts} 2^{-|p|} is a specific example of an algorithmic-random real. It is notable because:
opts: It is computable to arbitrary precision
It is left-computable (its binary expansion can be approximated from below) but not computable, and every bit encodes a halting problem
exp: Ω (halting probability) is Martin-Löf random, left-computable (Σ over terminating programs ≤ 1 by Kraft), but not computable. Knowing finitely many bits of Ω answers finitely many halting problems. It is the canonical example of an 'unknowable' real number.
